newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger women stage sit-in for release of detainees.
newsitem.headline: Niger women stage sit-in for release of detainees.

text.p: Several hundred women staged a sit-in on Sunday outside a police barracks in Niger's capital Niamey to demand the release of opposition militants arrested after turbulent protests last weekend, witnesses said.

Elsewhere, polling took place for three national assembly seats in two eastern constituencies where the supreme court scrapped the results of the November 23 parliamentary elections on grounds of fraud.

The women staging the sit-in were members of an eight-party alliance that accuses President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara of rigging the West African nation's July presidential poll to legitimise his rule after a January 1996 coup.
Three opposition leaders, including former president Mahamane Ousmane, the man Mainassara toppled, are being held on charges of threatening state security.

Mahamane, former parliament speaker Mahamadou Issoufou and Tandja Mamadou, leader of the former single party the National Movement for a Development Society (MNSD), were arrested after the banned January 11 protest.
Witnesses say up to 100 people have been arrested nationwide following the march which security forces broke up with tear gas. Officials speak of 62 arrests.
The marchers were seeking greater access to state media.
Former colonial power France and the United States, which condemned Mainassara's election as fraudulent, have urged the release of the three opposition leaders.
The opposition boycotted the November parliamentary poll in which Mainassara's supporters won a comfortable majority in the 83-seat national assembly.
